title: 己亥杂诗·其五
titlePy: Jǐ Hài Zá Shī · Qí Wǔ
titleEn: Miscellaneous Poems of the Year Jihai, No. 5
author: 龚自珍
intro: Leaving the capital in sadness, a poet sees fallen petals on the ground and finds hope in them: they are not heartless — they turn into spring soil and feed the flowers to come.
analysis: 1839年（己亥年），龚自珍辞官离开北京，这首诗写在离京的路上。前两句写离别：太阳西斜，离别的愁绪像水一样浩浩荡荡；他扬起马鞭向东一指，从此就是远在天涯了。后两句是全诗最有名的地方：诗人看到地上的落花，想到自己——花虽然落了，却不是没有感情的东西，它化成春天的泥土，还要保护、滋养新开的花。“落红”就是落花，诗人用它比喻自己：离开了官场，也还要为国家、为下一代出力。前面伤感，后面却很积极，情绪有一个大转变。现在人们常用“落红不是无情物，化作春泥更护花”来赞美老师、长辈默默奉献、培养后人。
analysisEn:
In 1839, the year called jǐhài in the traditional calendar, Gong Zizhen resigned from his post and left Beijing. He wrote this on the road. The first two lines are about parting: the sun is slanting low in the west, and his sorrow at leaving spreads out wide like a flood of water. He raises his riding whip and points east — from here on, he is at the far edge of the world.

The last two lines are the famous ones. He sees fallen petals (落红, literally “fallen red”) on the ground and thinks of himself. The flowers have dropped, but they are not things without feeling: they become spring soil and go on protecting the flowers that come after them. The fallen petals are a metaphor for the poet: he has left office, but he still means to serve his country and help the next generation.

So the mood turns around completely, from sadness to quiet hope. Today the couplet “Fallen petals are not heartless things; they turn to spring earth to nourish the flowers” is often quoted to praise teachers, parents and elders who give their lives to bringing up young people.
background: Gong Zizhen (1792–1841) was a Qing thinker and poet who called for reform as the empire declined. In 1839 he resigned and travelled south from Beijing, writing 315 short poems on the journey and after, the Miscellaneous Poems of the Year Jihai; this is No. 5.
pronunciation: 斜 xié（统编教材注 xié；古音读 xiá，与“涯”“花”押韵）。更 gèng；即 jí。
version: 采用统编教材文本（中学课外古诗词诵读篇目）。《己亥杂诗》共三百一十五首，这是第五首，网站收全首。

lines.py: hào dàng lí chóu bái rì xié
lines.lit: Vast and boundless, the sorrow of parting; the white sun slants;
lines.en: My grief at parting spreads wide as the sun sinks west;

lines.py: yín biān dōng zhǐ jí tiān yá
lines.lit: the poet’s whip points east — that is the edge of the sky.
lines.en: I point my whip to the east, and the far end of the world begins.

lines.py: luò hóng bù shì wú qíng wù
lines.lit: Fallen red is not a thing without feeling;
lines.en: Fallen petals are not heartless things —

lines.py: huà zuò chūn ní gèng hù huā
lines.lit: turning into spring mud, it further protects the flowers.
lines.en: they turn to spring earth and nourish the flowers to come.

words.note: 干支纪年，六十年一轮；现代农历仍用。
不定题目、随感而写的诗。

words.en: vast and mighty (like a great river)

words.note: 古诗常用词，现代汉语书面语偶尔用。

words.en: the edge of the sky; a faraway place
words.note: 现代汉语仍用，如“海角天涯”“天涯海角”。
红：指花。古语用法，现代汉语说“落花”。
现代汉语仍用，如“无情的人”。
现代汉语“保护”“爱护”“护士”。

imagery.name: 落花
imagery.zh: 落花化作春泥护花，比喻诗人离开官场后仍愿为国家和后人奉献。
imagery.en: Petals that turn to soil and feed new flowers stand for the poet, out of office but still serving the country and the young.

imagery.name: 白日
imagery.zh: 白日西斜写出离别的黄昏时刻，也暗示国家和诗人自己的处境都在走下坡路。
imagery.en: The slanting sun sets the hour of departure — and hints that both the poet’s career and the empire are in decline.
